title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering during regional failover
author: Priya Raman
description: Context: During a regional failover test we observed the SLO enforcer's backoff ordering queue emit non-deterministic ordering which led to bursty load-shedding in the new region and SLO violations. This was traced to a race in the enqueue path where an in-flight backoff timer could reinsert a request with an older priority key and a subsequent stale topology update could reorder queue priorities. Impact: production incidents (2026-02-19) showed short periods of elevated error budget burn in the EU region and increased customer errors for dedicated customers on high-concurrency routes. Goal: make a minimal, backward-compatible hotfix that stabilizes ordering and reduces probability of reordering races during topology changes and failover. What I changed: 1) Introduced a compare-and-swap guarded enqueue that tags backoff entries with a monotonic generation id derived from the topology/version handshake. 2) Added a small in-memory dedup filter on the queue insert path to ignore reinserts that are older than the current generation. 3) Tightened the backoff-timer cancellation path to ensure timers are drained before allowing topology-driven reinserts. 4) Added deterministic ordering unit tests and an integration test that simulates concurrent failover + backoff expiration. 5) Added an emergency ops flag (slo_enforcer.allow_reinserts=false) to allow rapid rollback to previous behavior without code changes. Notes on scope: This is intentionally scoped small to avoid touching the hot scheduling code paths. The change avoids large refactors; it uses an env-guarded flag and metrics to observe behavior post-merge.
commits: a1b2c3d: guard enqueue with generation id and dedup filter
d4e5f6a: ensure backoff timer cancellation drains before reinserts
b7c8d9e: add unit/integration tests for ordering + add ops flag and metrics
discussion: Evan Brooks (reviewer): Can you explain why we prefer generation ids over simply using timer sequence numbers? Is there any perf impact?

Author (Priya Raman): Generation ids map to the topology/version handshake (region agent). Sequence numbers are per-timer and can still collide when timers are cancelled and recreated; generation id guarantees monotonicity across topology updates. Measured overhead is ~30ns per enqueue in a synthetic microbenchmark, negligible compared to queue operations.
Marta Li (reviewer): Tests look good. One nit: please add a Prometheus metric for 'rejected_reinserts_due_to_generation' so SRE can monitor rollback impact.
Author: Added metric and exposed it under slo_enforcer.reinserts.rejected_generation_count (see observability/metrics change).
Diego Alvarez (approver): Verified integration test locally and ran a small chaos run. Approving after CI passes.
SRE on-call (comment): We observed the same sequence on the staging failover; with this patch the error budget spike did not reproduce in 3/3 runs. Will monitor tomorrow in EU canary rollout.
CI system: build-and-test passed (unit+integration), e2e flaky test rerun passed on second attempt.
release_notes: Hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer ordering during regional failover. Adds generation-guarded enqueue, dedup filter, timer drain, observability metric. Emergency ops flag for quick rollback.
